stem: An industrial engineering study measures the assembly time (seconds) for a sample of 20 factory workers. The sample mean is 187.0 sec with a sample standard deviation of 31.7 sec. However, 2 of the 20 observations appear to be outliers (values more than 2.5 standard deviations from the mean). If these outliers are removed, the remaining 18 observations have a mean of 179.2 sec and standard deviation of 20.4 sec. Estimate the true population mean and provide a 95% confidence interval that accounts for the uncertainty about whether outliers should be included.

ground_truth.answer: With all data: mean = 187.0, 95% CI = [172.2, 201.8]. Without outliers: mean = 179.2, 95% CI = [169.6, 188.8]. Combined interval accounting for analytic uncertainty: [169.6, 201.8]. Point estimate: 183.1 sec.

solution_steps: The outlier treatment choice creates structural uncertainty. Combined interval: [169.6, 201.8].
common_failure_modes: Using only the full sample without considering outlier impact
Removing outliers without reporting both analyses
Not recognizing that the choice of analysis method is itself a source of uncertainty
